A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeAutoDiff, retaining the latent-diffusion foundation and original six generation benchmarks. All pages, including appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial changes in scope.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation benchmarks, sampling measurements, component ablations and entity-conditioned results in Tables 2–3 and supplementary visualizations.

after.justification: v3 reports generation results plus original imputation, forecasting, metadata-conditioning, scalability, memorization and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: v3 replaces the explicit entity-label classifier-free guidance formulation with task-mask conditioning, a conditional decoder and conditional denoiser. It permits feature compression from F to L, removes the encoder's Transformer/convolution block and changes its stated RNN depth. These alter the procedure and architecture, beyond expanding their description.

E1.justification: The original six generation datasets remain, while v3 adds ETTh1, Energy, Bike Sharing and controlled synthetic datasets. Evaluation expands to direct forecasting, random and structured missing-data imputation, time-varying metadata conditioning and corrupted-metadata scenarios. The earlier explicit entity-conditioned evaluation is removed.

E2.justification: The five original generation comparators remain. Tables 12–14 introduce twelve evaluated imputation/forecasting baselines, including CSDI, TimeLLM, MOMENT, PatchTST, iTransformer and TimeMixer++ (TimeMixerPP in tables), although availability varies by setting. Timeweaver is discussed but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: v3 states T=48 for core generation versus v1's T=24 single-sequence setting, and reduces stated training from 50,000 to 25,000 epochs. New evaluations introduce 70/20/10 and 80/20 splits, MAE/MSE, structured masks and look-back windows of 12, 24 and 36. Appendix B still describes 200/177-length entity sequences, leaving some protocol correspondence unresolved; these reported changes do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v3 adds VAE-only/DDPM-only controls, alternative encoder/decoder and noise ablations, beta-scheduling and hyperparameter sweeps, compression/scalability studies, DCR memorization analysis, metadata-corruption tests and conditional case studies. The earlier Transformer/convolution ablation disappears alongside that component. These substantially expand the questions investigated.

E5.justification: Both versions already report means and standard deviations. Table 2's description changes from ten metric scores on one synthetic dataset to scores across ten generated datasets. Figure 13 additionally reports five independent runs and displays error bars. This changes reported replication practices without establishing additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive conditional-task, diagnostic and scalability results while removing C-TimeAutoDiff result rows. Most Table 2 means remain unchanged, but some reported deviations change: Diffusion-TS's AirQuality feature-correlation entry changes from 0.716(1.041) to 0.716(0.141). New findings include small-data replication in Figure 8 and dataset-dependent imputation performance in Tables 12–14. These additions do not establish same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's VAE/DDPM objectives and DDPM background, v3 introduces formal task-mask definitions, a conditional generative factorization and an ELBO derivation in Section 4.1 and Appendix A. Appendix G adds component-wise training and inference complexity analysis. These are substantive mathematical additions.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from heterogeneous sequence synthesis with entity conditioning to a unified framework for generation, imputation, forecasting and time-varying metadata conditioning. The abstract adds feature-compression, downstream-error, conditional scenario-exploration and data-dependent generalization claims. Imputation, previously future work, becomes a claimed demonstrated capability.

C2.justification: v3 interprets memorization as data-regime dependent, explicitly identifying replication on Hurricane and AirQuality. It adds hypotheses about temporal modeling in both stages, explanations of weaker Bike Sharing imputation, compression tradeoffs and metadata-noise sensitivity. Section 6 expands interpretability and conditional-bias limitations; formal privacy guarantees remain prospective.

D1.justification: v3 replaces code-on-request instructions with a reported public repository and identifies PyPOTS and ImputeEval.py for baseline settings. Appendix F adds optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, EMA, diffusion-step and noise-schedule details; other appendices add processing instructions and runtime/memory measurements. However, v1's explicit CPU/RTX 2080 hardware description is removed.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially beyond generation methods to forecasting, imputation, metadata conditioning and foundation models. Section 2 and Appendix D position TimeAutoDiff against Timeweaver, MOMENT, Chronos and TimesFM, while elaborating distinctions from retained tabular and time-series diffusion methods. This changes research positioning beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Related work and problem setting become standalone sections; methods gain an objective-first organization and explicit training/inference subsections. Experiments are reorganized by task, metric explanations move to the appendix, and the discussion is substantially recast.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the architecture diagrams and adds task-mask and conditional-decoder schematics. Earlier marginal-distribution panels are replaced by extensive autocorrelation, memorization, conditional-trajectory and robustness displays. Benchmark and ablation tables are restructured and separated, with additional comparison tables and a new publication layout.

improvement.justification: v3 adds valuable diagnostic controls, a memorization audit absent from v1 and fuller reproducibility information. However, central reporting remains unresolved: Table 2 retains almost all means despite changed stated settings, and Table 12 reports Bike Sharing MCAR MAE 0.4620 with MSE 0.0996, incompatible with standard same-sample metrics, which require MSE >= MAE squared. The PDFs provide no explanation. These concerns affect the expanded empirical claims, preventing a reliable net judgment against the substantial benefits.
